import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Read the data
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')

# Create a figure with multiple subplots
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 12))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(3, 3, hspace=0.3, wspace=0.3)

# 1. Income Distribution by Education
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 0])
education_order = df['Education'].value_counts().index
sns.boxplot(data=df, y='Education', x='Income', order=education_order, ax=ax1, palette='Set2')
ax1.set_title('Income Distribution by Education', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_xlabel('Income')

# 2. Age Distribution
ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 1])
current_year = 2014  # Based on customer dates
df['Age'] = current_year - df['Year_Birth']
ax2.hist(df['Age'], bins=20, color='skyblue', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax2.set_title('Age Distribution of Customers', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_xlabel('Age')
ax2.set_ylabel('Frequency')

# 3. Total Spending by Category
ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 2])
spending_cols = ['MntWines', 'MntFruits', 'MntMeatProducts', 
                 'MntFishProducts', 'MntSweetProducts', 'MntGoldProds']
total_spending = df[spending_cols].sum()
colors = plt.cm.Set3(range(len(spending_cols)))
wedges, texts, autotexts = ax3.pie(total_spending, labels=['Wines', 'Fruits', 'Meat', 'Fish', 'Sweets', 'Gold'], 
                                     autopct='%1.1f%%', colors=colors, startangle=90)
ax3.set_title('Total Spending by Product Category', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')

# 4. Marital Status Distribution
ax4 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 0])
marital_counts = df['Marital_Status'].value_counts()
ax4.bar(marital_counts.index, marital_counts.values, color='coral', alpha=0.7, edgecolor='black')
ax4.set_title('Customer Marital Status', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax4.set_xlabel('Marital Status')
ax4.set_ylabel('Count')
ax4.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 5. Income vs Total Spending
ax5 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 1])
df['TotalSpending'] = df[spending_cols].sum(axis=1)
ax5.scatter(df['Income'], df['TotalSpending'], alpha=0.6, c=df['Age'], cmap='viridis', s=50)
ax5.set_title('Income vs Total Spending', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax5.set_xlabel('Income')
ax5.set_ylabel('Total Spending')
cbar = plt.colorbar(ax5.collections[0], ax=ax5)
cbar.set_label('Age', rotation=270, labelpad=15)

# 6. Purchase Channels
ax6 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 2])
purchase_channels = ['NumWebPurchases', 'NumCatalogPurchases', 'NumStorePurchases']
channel_totals = df[purchase_channels].sum()
ax6.bar(['Web', 'Catalog', 'Store'], channel_totals, color=['#FF6B6B', '#4ECDC4', '#45B7D1'], 
        alpha=0.8, edgecolor='black')
ax6.set_title('Total Purchases by Channel', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax6.set_ylabel('Number of Purchases')

# 7. Kids at Home vs Spending
ax7 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 0])
df['TotalKids'] = df['Kidhome'] + df['Teenhome']
kids_spending = df.groupby('TotalKids')['TotalSpending'].mean()
ax7.bar(kids_spending.index, kids_spending.values, color='lightgreen', alpha=0.7, edgecolor='black')
ax7.set_title('Average Spending by Number of Kids', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax7.set_xlabel('Number of Kids at Home')
ax7.set_ylabel('Average Total Spending')

# 8. Campaign Response Rate
ax8 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 1])
campaign_cols = ['AcceptedCmp1', 'AcceptedCmp2', 'AcceptedCmp3', 'AcceptedCmp4', 'AcceptedCmp5', 'Response']
campaign_acceptance = df[campaign_cols].sum()
ax8.barh(['Cmp1', 'Cmp2', 'Cmp3', 'Cmp4', 'Cmp5', 'Response'], 
         campaign_acceptance, color='mediumpurple', alpha=0.7, edgecolor='black')
ax8.set_title('Campaign Acceptance Rates', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax8.set_xlabel('Number of Acceptances')

# 9. Recency vs Web Visits
ax9 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 2])
ax9.scatter(df['Recency'], df['NumWebVisitsMonth'], alpha=0.6, color='orange', s=50)
ax9.set_title('Recency vs Web Visits per Month', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax9.set_xlabel('Recency (days)')
ax9.set_ylabel('Web Visits per Month')

# Add main title
fig.suptitle('Customer Marketing Campaign Analysis Dashboard', 
             fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=0.995)

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()
